_note: Terrain grid for the Canadian Rails 1851 map. 22 rows x 26 cols, pointy-top odd-r (odd rows shifted right), hex radius 34 rather than the American board's 41 — the smaller tile buys 44% more cells inside the same 1700x1400 frame, which is what pulls the crowded Lake Erie and Lake Ontario shores apart. Legend: O = off-map (ocean, lake, or panel space), P = plains, F = forest, M = mountain, C = city (the city itself comes from cities.json, which must place a city on every C). Two areas are deliberately empty: the top-left (rows 0-4, cols 0-11) is the Shield cut back to a rim, and now carries the title cartouche; rows 15-21 carry the year track, terrain legend and house supply, with the Atlantic corner (cols 19-25, rows 12+) carrying the action table.

regions._note: Why each area is the terrain it is. Purely documentation — the generator reads only `grid`.
regions.Canadian Shield: Rows 0-6, cols 1-9. Mountain. Settlement in Canada West had run up against the Shield in exactly 1851; the government began surveying the Ottawa-Huron Tract that decade. This is the northern wall.
regions.Laurentians / north shore: Rows 1-4, cols 9-12. Mountain. The Shield comes right down to the St Lawrence below Québec — the reason the Côte-Nord was never settled.
regions.Ottawa Valley: Rows 3-7, cols 6-8. Forest. The great square-timber pineries that made Bytown.
regions.St Lawrence Lowlands: Rows 5-9, cols 6-11. Plains. The seigneurial farmland and the one cheap corridor between the two barriers — the trunk route.
regions.Ontario peninsula: Rows 9-12, cols 1-5. Plains and cities. The best farmland in British North America and the densest town network; the Great Western's battleground.
regions.Frontenac Axis: (6,8) and (7,8), mountain, immediately north of Kingston. The Shield reaches the St Lawrence here — a genuine narrows in the corridor.
regions.Notre-Dame Mountains: Rows 2-5, cols 13-14 and rows 7-9, cols 11-12. Mountain. The Appalachian chain along the south shore, continuing into the Eastern Townships as the Sutton range.
regions.Matapédia gap: (14,3) and (14,4), mountain, between Campbellton and the lower St Lawrence. The only land route from Canada East into New Brunswick, and the line Major Robinson recommended in 1849.
regions.New Brunswick Highlands: Rows 5-8, cols 12-13. Mountain and forest. The interior barrier between the Saint John valley and the Miramichi.
regions.Maritime Plain: (16,6) and (16,7). Plains. The low ground from Fredericton through The Bend to the Northumberland shore.
regions.Chignecto Isthmus: The Bend (17,6) to Amherst (17,7). The 24 km neck that is the only land connection into Nova Scotia.
regions.Cobequid Hills: (18,6), mountain, between Amherst and Pictou. The ridge the Nova Scotia Railway had to work around.
regions.Annapolis Valley: (17,8), plains, sheltered between North and South Mountain.
regions.Cape Breton: (20,7) mountain highlands, Sydney (21,6) at the coalfield. Attached only across the Strait of Canso at (20,6).
regions.Prince Edward Island: Charlottetown (18,5), reachable only from Pictou (19,6) across the Northumberland Strait — the 1851 packet route. A deliberate island prize; see the design brief.
